https://www.azernews.az/region/265227.ht.body: Russia warns US-backed AI data centre could strain Armenia's electricity supply 9 October 2026 12:18 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Russia has raised concerns over the development of a new artificial intelligence data centre in Armenia, warning that plans to expand the facility's capacity could place considerable pressure on the country's electricity system and potentially lead to power shortages. Aleksey Shevtsov, deputy secretary of Russia's Security Council, questioned the necessity of the Firebird AI data centre in the Armenian city of Hrazdan, which uses Western technology, including processors manufactured by US semiconductor company NVIDIA. Speaking to reporters, Shevtsov argued that Armenia already possesses sufficient data storage infrastructure to meet its domestic requirements. “This civilian facility is clearly unnecessary for Armenia's domestic needs, since the OVIO data center, owned by Rostelecom [company of Russia], has been operating in the country since 2024, which fully covers the needs of commercial and state institutions in terms of data storage,” he said. The Russian official's remarks come amid plans by Firebird AI to substantially expand its computing infrastructure in Armenia, with the company reportedly targeting a capacity of 300 megawatts (MW) at its Hrazdan complex by the end of 2027. Shevtsov drew attention to the scale of the proposed expansion, comparing its projected electricity requirements with Armenia's overall winter power demand. According to the Russian official, the planned capacity “is nearly a quarter of the load [i.e. 1.3 GW] on Armenia’s power system during the winter period.” “Thus, by calculating the announced plans, additional energy capacity will be required [in Armenia] to maintain the [aforesaid] center’s operation,” he added. Shevtsov further warned that the development of energy-intensive computing facilities could create additional challenges for Armenia's electricity supply. In his assessment, “amid growing needs, including the strengthening of the data center, Armenia may face a serious electricity deficit, which will inevitably affect [the country’s] ordinary citizens.” The concerns reflect the substantial electricity requirements associated with large-scale AI computing infrastructure, particularly facilities equipped with high-performance processors used to train and operate artificial intelligence models. However, the projected 300 MW capacity does not necessarily mean the facility would continuously consume that amount of electricity. Its actual impact on Armenia's power system would depend on operational demand, the pace of expansion, available generation capacity and investments in electricity infrastructure. https://24.kg/en/article/kyrgyz-troops-h.body: Military personnel from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia and Tajikistan have begun arriving in Belarus to take part in command-and-staff exercises organized by the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). The drills will run from October 12 to 16, the Belarusian Defense Ministry reported. Two exercises will be held in Belarus: Indestructible Brotherhood-2026 and Barrier-2026. Both are part of the planned training of collective security forces and cover several areas of operation. During Indestructible Brotherhood-2026, participants will practice preparations for a peacekeeping operation. Under Barrier-2026, military personnel and specialists will work on tasks related to eliminating sources of biological threats. Over the five days, peacekeeping and specialized training activities will take place simultaneously at military training grounds and other facilities across Belarus. The Belarusian Defense Ministry stressed that the exercises are part of routine training, are not directed against any third country and are not linked to heightened tensions in any region.

https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-09/en.body: Photo: Unsplash, photo editor: Dastan Shanay Visitors from China spent an average of about 467,000 tenge (approximately $1,040) during trips to Kazakhstan, compared with about 161,000 tenge for visitors from Russia. A significant share of Chinese visitors’ spending went toward international transportation, according to data from Kazakhstan’s Bureau of National Statistics (BNS) . According to a sample survey of inbound visitors covering January-July 2026, the total expenditure of 763 visitors from China amounted to 356.3 million tenge. Therefore, the average expenditure per person was around 467,000 tenge (approximately $1,040). For comparison, 12,757 surveyed visitors from Russia spent 2.05 billion tenge in total. Spending per person averaged about 161,000 tenge, 2.9 times less than visitors from China. At the same time, visitors from Russia accounted for more than half of all survey participants. The BNS surveyed 25,000 foreign visitors, 51% of whom were from Russia. Visitors from China accounted for around 3%. W hat visitors from China spent their money on International transportation accounted for the largest share of spending by visitors from China. They spent 238 million tenge on travel to and from Kazakhstan, representing 66.8% of their total expenditure. Accommodation accounted for 41.1 million tenge, while food and groceries came to 34.9 million and purchases of goods to 15.8 million. Domestic transportation expenses totaled 11.2 million tenge. The spending patterns of visitors from Russia differed significantly. International transportation accounted for 861.7 million tenge, or 42% of their total expenditure. Food and groceries accounted for 448.5 million tenge, purchases of goods for 296.4 million tenge, and accommodation for 243.1 million tenge. Thus, international transportation costs account for much of the difference in average spending between visitors from the two countries. Excluding international transportation, average spending per person would come to around 155,000 tenge for visitors from China and 93,000 tenge for those from Russia, narrowing the difference from 2.9 times to 1.7 times. At the same time, international transportation spending does not necessarily go to Kazakhstani companies, as foreign carriers may operate some trips. Nearly half of visitors from China come to Kazakhstan for business BNS data also provides a breakdown of visitors by purpose of visit. Among those surveyed from China, 358 people (46.9%) came to Kazakhstan for business and professional purposes. Another 405 cited personal reasons. The share of business trips among visitors from Russia was significantly lower. Of the 12,757 people surveyed, 2,376 (18.6%) visited Kazakhstan for business and professional purposes, while the remaining 10,381 came for personal reasons. The average length of stay also differed. Visitors from China spent 2,540 nights in Kazakhstan, averaging 3.3 nights per person. For visitors from Russia, the figure was around 3.5 nights. With comparable lengths of stay, visitors from China spent more on average than visitors from Russia, while nearly half traveled to Kazakhstan for business. The BNS survey was conducted among non-residents departing Kazakhstan at airports, railway stations, long-distance bus stations, and land border checkpoints. The survey included 25,001 people. Their combined expenditure amounted to 4.88 billion tenge, of which around 2.4 billion tenge went towards international transportation. However, these figures reflect survey participants’ spending, not that of all foreign visitors to Kazakhstan over the first seven months of 2026. https://24.kg/en/article/uk-imposes-sanc.body: The United Kingdom imposed sanctions on three companies registered in Kyrgyzstan on October 8. The new restrictions were published in an official sanctions notice issued by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The sanctions target Processing KG OJSC, TokenSpot CJSC and Tsunami Payments LLC, as well as Processing KG Director Ulan Bukabaev. The Ministry of Finance of Kyrgyzstan is the sole shareholder of Processing KG. Four entries were added to the UK sanctions list under its Russia sanctions regime. Processing KG was assigned the identifier RUS3756. The company is subject to asset freezes, restrictions on trust services and director-related activities, and internet services restrictions. The measures also prohibit UK credit and financial institutions from establishing or maintaining correspondent banking relationships with the company and ban the processing of payments to, by, or through it. The UK sanctions record identifies Kyrgyzstan’s Ministry of Finance as the company’s parent entity. The British authorities said there were reasonable grounds to suspect that Processing KG was involved in activities that benefit or support the Russian government by conducting business in a sector of economic significance to the Russian state. The sanctions record lists two websites associated with Processing KG: processing-kg. com and vexpay.net. This directly links the VexPay payment platform to Processing KG in the UK sanctions listing. Processing KG Director Ulan Arymbaevich Bukabaev was also subjected to individual sanctions, including an asset freeze, a travel ban, restrictions on trust services and restrictions on holding director positions in the UK. The UK cited his role as director of Processing KG as the grounds for the measures. The list also includes Bishkek-registered TokenSpot CJSC, assigned the identifier RUS3758. The company faces the same main set of financial restrictions. The UK government said there were reasonable grounds to suspect that TokenSpot benefits or supports the Russian government through activities in Russia’s financial sector, which the UK considers a strategically significant industry. Related news Liquidation initiated for 35 legal entities to minimise sanctions risks The third Kyrgyzstan-registered company added to the UK sanctions list is Tsunami Payments LLC, which was assigned the identifier RUS3763. The UK authorities cited the company’s alleged activities in Russia’s financial sector as the grounds for the decision. Tsunami Payments was registered in Kyrgyzstan in February 2024. In June of the same year, the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan issued the company two licenses. One authorizes it to process and clear third-party payments and settlements. The other allows it to accept and process payments and settlements for goods and services through payment systems.

https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.body: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Kazakhstan to expand Russia border checkpoint capacity Kazakhstan News 9 October 2026 12:25 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Unsplash /Imre Tomosvari Fuad Namazov Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 9. Kazakhstan is reconstructing the Syrym checkpoint on its border with Russia to increase its capacity and improve the efficiency of border crossings. This was reflected in a press release issued today by the joint-stock company KazAvtoZhol. “Reconstruction work is being carried out in two shifts at the Syrym checkpoint, located on the border between the West Kazakhstan Region and the Russian Federation,” the publication says. The project aims to modernize the checkpoint's infrastructure, increase its throughput capacity, and create more comfortable conditions for citizens and vehicles. The company added that works are proceeding according to the approved schedule. The project is expected to improve the checkpoint's infrastructure and make border crossings more efficient. Notably, Kazakhstan and Russia are pursuing a broader modernization of their shared border infrastructure to increase freight capacity and streamline cross-border transport. Kazakhstan plans to modernize 30 road checkpoints along its border with Russia, with construction at three facilities, including the Syrym-Mashtakovo crossing, scheduled for completion by the end of 2026. Work at the remaining checkpoints is expected to be completed in 2027. The two countries are also advancing digital transport procedures, including electronic permits, data exchange between inspection systems and electronic queue management. Kazakhstan's CarGoRuqsat electronic queue system has been introduced at 24 checkpoints on the Russian border. In May 2026, the countries also signed a joint action plan on transport digitalization and reported progress in developing automated freight transport and the North-South International Transport Corridor. Russia, meanwhile, plans to modernize 10 priority road checkpoints on its border with Kazakhstan by 2030, aiming to increase their combined capacity to 3.5 million trucks annually. Sayfiddin Karaev , asia+ 09.10.2026 15:05 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL Tajikistan and the United States have discussed petroleum product supplies to Tajikistan’s domestic market. The issue was raised at a meeting between Energy and Water Resources Minister Daler Juma and the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Dushanbe, Ms. Carson Relitz Rocker in Dushanbe on October 8. According to Tajikistan’s Ministry of Energy and Water Resources (MoEWR), the meeting focused on bilateral cooperation in energy and water resources and prospects for expanding mutually beneficial ties. The parties also discussed the situation on Tajikistan’s domestic market and the supply of petroleum products. The ministry did not specify which supply issues were discussed, whether alternative import sources were considered or whether any concrete agreements were reached. Both sides expressed their readiness to continue dialogue and strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, the ministry said. How much fuel does Tajikistan import? In January–September 2026, Tajikistan imported approximately 1.37 million tons of oil, petroleum products, liquefied gases and other related goods worth a total of $1.13 billion, according to foreign trade statistics. The main imports included: Diesel fuel: 424,800 tons worth $399.1 million. Motor petrol: 333,200 tons worth $292.2 million. Liquefied gases: 321,300 tons worth $218.9 million. Kerosene, including aviation fuel: 50,700 tons worth $56.2 million. The total also included lubricants, bitumen, petroleum coke and other petroleum products. Which countries supply Tajikistan with fuel? Russia remains Tajikistan’s main supplier of petroleum products. In the first nine months of 2026, Tajikistan imported around 708,000 tons of petroleum products from Russia, worth $628.9 million. Russian supplies accounted for 73.2% of the total import value in this category. Turkmenistan ranked second, supplying 100,300 tons worth $117.4 million. Other suppliers included Uzbekistan, with 36,200 tons worth $38.1 million; Belarus, with 19,700 tons worth $21.4 million; Iran, with 15,600 tons worth $14.7 million; Kazakhstan, with 9,100 tons worth $9 million; and Kyrgyzstan, with 10,200 tons worth $4.2 million. Kazakhstan is also Tajikistan’s main supplier of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). In January–September, Tajikistan imported around 225,600 tons of LPG from Kazakhstan worth $153.8 million. Russia supplied another 94,800 tons of LPG worth $64.6 million during the same period. Join us on social media! https://www.trend.az/casia/turkmenistan/.body: Home Central Asia Turkmenistan Vladimir Putin, Serdar Berdimuhamedov discuss Turkmenistan-Russia cooperation Turkmenistan News 9 October 2026 10:26 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Turkmenistan Today (TDH) Fuad Namazov Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 9. Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Turkmenistan’s Avaza on October 8 to discuss bilateral cooperation, including trade, the economy and cultural ties. This was reflected in a press release published by the Turkmen Foreign Ministry today. According to the information, the meeting took place during Putin’s visit to Turkmenistan to participate in high-level international events in the National Tourist Zone of Avaza, including the meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Caspian Environmental Summit. The two presidents discussed political and diplomatic relations, with an emphasis on regular high-level contacts and coordination on bilateral issues. Trade and economic cooperation was also identified as an important area of bilateral engagement. The sides also highlighted cooperation in education, healthcare, science and culture. “We highly value your personal attention to the development of regional cooperation and view the meetings in Avaza as an opportunity for an open exchange of views, the formulation of joint approaches, and the definition of new areas of interaction,” Berdimuhamedov said. He also reaffirmed Turkmenistan’s readiness to continue comprehensive cooperation with Russia, expressing confidence that bilateral relations would continue to develop for the benefit of both countries, according to the ministry. Putin thanked the Turkmen side for its hospitality and invitation to the international events, and conveyed greetings to Chairman of Turkmenistan’s Halk Maslahaty Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov. Meanwhile, Russia and Turkmenistan maintain a strategic partnership covering trade, energy, transport, diplomacy and humanitarian ties. Russia remains one of Turkmenistan’s key trading partners, with bilateral trade exceeding $1.6 billion annually, according to Turkmen government data. In 2025, bilateral trade continued to expand, with trade turnover rising 21.4% in the first quarter, while the two sides worked on an intergovernmental action plan for 2025-2027. Cooperation also extends to the fuel and energy sector, industry, agriculture, banking and finance, and digital technologies. At the political level, Moscow and Ashgabat cooperate through the UN, CIS, the Caspian littoral states and the Central Asia-Russia format. In September 2026, Turkmenistan said preparations were underway for the 14th meeting of the bilateral intergovernmental commission, with the agenda covering trade, energy, transport, finance, industry and other areas. https://www.trend.az/casia/uzbekistan/42.body: Home Central Asia Uzbekistan Uzbekistan gas imports from Russia, Turkmenistan hit $1.21B in eight months Uzbekistan Analysis 9 October 2026 05:27 (UTC +04:00) Photo: The Ministry of Energy of Uzbekistan Niljan Bakhshaliyeva Uzbekistan Economics Correspondent Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 9. Uzbekistan increased its gas imports from Russia and Turkmenistan by 15.2% year on year to $1.21 billion in January–August 2026, while domestic natural gas production continued to decline. This is reflected in data from Uzbekistan’s National Statistics Committee. According to the committee, the value of gas imports increased by approximately $160 million compared with an estimated $1.05 billion in the same period of 2025. At the same time, Uzbekistan’s gas exports fell sharply. The country exported gas worth $322.3 million in January–August 2026, down approximately $172 million, or 34.8%, from the same period a year earlier. The contrasting trends in imports and exports come as domestic natural gas production continues to decline. Uzbekistan produced 24.2 billion cubic meters of natural gas during the first eight months of 2026, a decrease of 4.7 billion cubic meters, or 16.3%, from the same period in 2025. The figures point to a widening gap between domestic gas production and demand, increasing the role of imported supplies in Uzbekistan’s energy market. Russia has become an important source of additional gas supplies for Uzbekistan. Russian energy giant Gazprom supplied 6.5 billion cubic meters of natural gas to Uzbekistan in 2025. Uzbekistan has been seeking to diversify its gas supply sources and strengthen regional energy cooperation as declining domestic production creates additional demand for imported supplies. According to Trend 's calculations, the value of Uzbekistan’s gas imports from Russia and Turkmenistan increased by approximately $160 million year on year, from an estimated $1.05 billion in January–August 2025 to $1.21 billion in the same period of 2026. Meanwhile, gas exports declined by approximately $172 million, from an estimated $494 million to $322.3 million. As a result, Uzbekistan’s gas trade deficit widened from about $556 million to $887.7 million, an increase of approximately $332 million, or 60%. At the same time, domestic natural gas production fell by about 4.7 billion cubic meters, from an estimated 28.9 billion cubic meters to 24.2 billion cubic meters. https://24.kg/en/article/man-detained-fo.body: Police in Bishkek have identified and detained a man who hit a young man at the intersection of Chui Avenue and Fuchik Street. A video of the incident was shared on social media. The footage shows the man greeting one of the young men before gesturing for them to follow him. When the young man attempts to refuse, the man strikes him on the head. The young men are believed to be foreign nationals. Блок YouTube According to the Internal Affairs Department of Leninsky district, officers discovered the video while monitoring social media on October 6. The incident was registered, and police identified the man involved. The suspect, 52, was taken to the district police department. A report was drawn up against him under Article 126, "Petty Hooliganism, ” of the Code of Offences. He was placed in a temporary detention facility. The case materials will be submitted to court for a decision.

https://24.kg/en/article/customs-inspect.body: The State Committee for National Security (SCNS) of Kyrgyzstan has detained an inspector of the North-Eastern Customs on suspicion of abuse of office and misdeclaration of goods. According to the SCNS,a shipment of 98 lighting poles was cleared through customs under the guise of ferrous metal. An incorrect code from the Foreign Economic Activity Commodity Nomenclature was used during customs clearance, resulting in lost customs revenue and particularly large-scale damage to the state, the SCNS said. The detainee has been placed in the detention facility. The investigation is ongoing.

https://24.kg/en/article/relatives-of-me.body: Relatives of men accused or convicted of sexual offences against minors held a rally in Maxim Gorky Park in Bishkek on October 8. They called for their relatives’ cases to be reviewed and the quality of investigations to be examined. One of the speakers claimed that up to 90 percent of criminal cases of this kind opened since 2024 were «fabricated.» He alleged that in some cases, underage girls conceal their actual age and later demand money. However, no official data was presented to substantiate the figure of 90 percent cited at the rally. The claim reflects the position of a rally participant and has not been established as fact by law enforcement authorities. Блок YouTube In spring 2026, MP Ismanali Zhoroev reported receiving a collective appeal from relatives of people prosecuted under Articles 154, 155, 157 and 158 of the Criminal Code. At the time, around 500 people were said to be planning a peaceful rally in Gorky Park. The issue was discussed by a parliamentary committee in June. A representative of relatives of about 90 convicted men complained to lawmakers about the quality of investigations into sexual offences. The committee decided to send an inquiry to the Prosecutor General’s Office. The Interior Ministry issued a separate statement, urging the public not to question the work of investigators and courts in such cases without sufficient grounds. MP Aisarakаn Abdibaeva proposed discussing the use of probation supervision for certain offences under Part 1 of Article 154, «Rape, ” and Article 157, «Sexual Acts with a Child Under 16, ” as well as the possible reinstatement of reconciliation between the parties and consideration of circumstances in which a defendant claims not to have known the teenager’s actual age. Abdibaeva later said her remarks had been misinterpreted. She stressed that she had not proposed reducing penalties for pedophiles or people who commit violence against children, explaining that she had relayed complaints received from citizens and public organizations. According to the MP, representatives of the public association Ukuk Korgoo approached her on May 26 with concerns about the application of Articles 154–158 of the Criminal Code. They said the organization had received complaints from parents of convicted men in various parts of the country. Following Abdibaeva’s remarks, an online petition calling for her parliamentary mandate to be revoked collected around 30,000 signatures. She subsequently said she intended to appeal to the State Committee for National Security over what she described as the spread of misleading information about her position. In recent years, Kyrgyzstan has tightened its legislation on sexual offences against children. In particular, the law has restricted the possibility of terminating cases through reconciliation and the use of certain mechanisms for exemption from punishment. Meanwhile, official statistics do not substantiate claims that such cases are being fabricated on a widespread scale. For example, the Prosecutor’s Office of Sverdlovsky district reported that, in the first quarter of 2026, investigators were handling 50 criminal cases involving offences against minors and offences committed by adolescents. Some cases were referred to court, others were terminated or suspended, while the remainder were still under investigation.

https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/0.body: Former vice-chairman of Xinjiang regional government prosecuted on bribery counts - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Former vice-chairman of Xinjiang regional government prosecuted on bribery counts By Yang Zekun | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-10-09 13:22 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Chen Weijun, former vice-chairman of the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous regional government, has been prosecuted on charges of bribery , the Supreme People's Procuratorate said on Friday. The case was investigated by the National Commission of Supervision before being transferred to prosecutors for review and prosecution. The SPP approved Chen's arrest on suspicion of accepting bribes and designated the Chuzhou People's Procuratorate in Anhui province to handle the case. Chen was also a former member of the Standing Committee of the Communist Party of China Xinjiang Uygur autonomous regional committee. The Chuzhou procuratorate recently filed an indictment against Chen with the Chuzhou Intermediate People's Court, according to the SPP. Prosecutors alleged that Chen took advantage of a series of senior positions he held in Zhejiang province and Xinjiang to seek benefits for others and illegally accepted an especially large amount of money and valuables in return. The positions cited in the indictment include mayor and Party chief of Huzhou, vice-governor of Zhejiang, Party chief of Wenzhou, member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee, and member of the standing committee of the CPC Xinjiang Uygur autonomous regional committee and vice-chairman of the regional government. Prosecutors said Chen should be held criminally responsible for bribery. During the review and prosecution process, prosecutors informed Chen of his procedural rights, questioned him , and heard opinions from his defense counsel, the SPP said. Chen, 60, a native of Zhejiang province, began his career in 1986 and spent more than three decades working in Zhejiang. He served in a number of senior local and provincial posts, including mayor and Party chief of Huzhou, Party chief of Wenzhou , and vice-governor. He was transferred to Xinjiang in May 2021 and later served as a member of the regional Party committee's standing committee and executive vice-chairman of the regional government. Chen was placed under investigation in November 2025 and was expelled from the CPC and dismissed from public office in June 2026. Anti-graft authorities said Chen resisted investigation, failed to truthfully report personal matters, engaged in profit-making activities , and allowed relatives to use his influence for private gain. He was also accused of seeking benefits for others in personnel appointments, land use, tax and fee reductions , and construction contracts in exchange for large amounts of money and valuables. His suspected criminal offenses were subsequently transferred to procuratorial authorities for review and prosecution. https://24.kg/article/v-bishkeke-obsuzhd.body: В Бишкеке началась 26-я Центральноазиатская конференция по СМИ, организованная офисом представителя ОБСЕ по вопросам свободы СМИ. Главная тема форума — «Формирование общего информационного пространства: достоверность информации, медиаэтика и доверие в цифровую эпоху». В конференции участвуют более 120 представителей государственных органов, СМИ, гражданского общества, академического сообщества и международных экспертов из Кыргызстана, Казахстана, Монголии, Таджикистана, Туркменистана и Узбекистана. Участники обсуждают свободу СМИ, профессиональную этику журналистики, противодействие дезинформации, развитие медиаграмотности и укрепление доверия в обществе. С приветственным словом выступила заместитель министра культуры, информации и молодежной политики Салкын Сарногоева. Она отметила важность регионального сотрудничества для развития свободного и ответственного информационного пространства, доступа граждан к достоверной информации и защиты свободы слова. В ходе конференции обсуждаются изменения медиасреды в цифровую эпоху, необходимость развития критического мышления и культуры ответственного потребления информации. Организаторы отмечают, что форум должен стать площадкой для обмена опытом, обсуждения актуальных вызовов и выработки общих подходов к развитию регионального информационного пространства.

https://iz.ru/2181342/2026-10-09/tramp-p.body: Президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что не будет атаковать Иран, пока не пройдут выборы в конгресс, намеченные на 3 ноября. При этом Пентагон подготовил план трехдневных ударов по военным объектам Исламской Республики. Обещание Трампа привело к снижению цен на нефть. Как СМИ реагируют на действия Белого дома — в дайджесте «Известий». Reuters: Трамп отказался атаковать Иран до выборов в конгресс Трамп заявил, что США не будут наносить удар по Ирану до ноябрьских промежуточных выборов в конгресс, отметив, что две страны ведут «продуктивные» переговоры о прекращении войны, которая длится уже полгода. Она привела к снижению рейтинга одобрения Трампа и стала тяжелым бременем для его однопартийцев-республиканцев, пытающихся сохранить незначительное большинство в законодательных органах по итогам ноябрьских выборов. Reuters «Мы ведем продуктивные переговоры с Исламской Республикой Иран, — написал Трамп в социальной сети Truth Social. — Мы не будем нападать на Иран в период до промежуточных выборов, которые пройдут в США 3 ноября». Согласно недавнему опросу Reuters/Ipsos, около 60% американцев, включая каждого четвертого республиканца, не одобряют действия Трампа в отношении Ирана. Конфликт спровоцировал резкий рост цен на бензин в то время, когда избиратели называют стоимость жизни своей главной проблемой. Трамп неоднократно заявлял, что ожидает снижения цен на нефть после выборов, однако не представил детального плана выхода из войны. В последние недели Иран и США обменивались предложениями, направленными на прекращение войны и разблокирование Ормузского пролива — важнейшего маршрута транспортировки энергоносителей. Трамп отверг последнее предложение Тегерана. The New York Times: Пентагон разрабатывает новые планы ударов по Ирану По словам американских чиновников, военные готовят варианты возобновления крупных боевых действий против Ирана, несмотря на то, что Трамп продолжает проявлять неопределенность в отношении возобновления войны. Вскоре на Ближнем Востоке окажутся три авианосца, что станет мощной концентрацией сил, и Пентагон по приказу Трампа разработал планы по нанесению ударов по иранскому арсеналу беспилотников и ракет, энергетическим объектам и другим военным объектам. The New York Times По словам официальных лиц, в последние месяцы команда Трампа по национальной безопасности и Пентагон пять раз представляли ему предложения по проведению крупных операций против Ирана или хуситов — поддерживаемой Ираном ополченческой группировки, базирующейся в Йемене. Каждый раз Трамп накладывал вето на эти планы. Но Трамп в очередной раз распорядился разработать варианты нанесения удара. Высокопоставленные чиновники по вопросам национальной безопасности во главе с вице-президентом Джей Ди Вэнсом обсудили планы на встрече в Кэмп-Дэвиде 2 октября. По словам источников, знакомых с предложением, планы сосредоточены на короткой, но интенсивной кампании, которая продлится около трех дней. Рейтинговый отсчет: могут ли США нанести удары по Ирану до выборов в конгресс Эскалация конфликта вряд ли поможет Дональду Трампу в преддверии голосования CNN: почему Трамп и Иран ждут результатов промежуточных выборов Заявление Трампа о том, что он не будет снова нападать на Иран до промежуточных выборов, стало негласным признанием ущерба, наносимого надеждам республиканцев войной, которая противоречит его обещанию быстрой победы. Противодействие конфликту и недовольство высокими ценами на бензин и дизельное топливо, которые он вызвал, являются одной из главных причин, по которой Республиканская партия сталкивается с трудностями или напряженной борьбой за места в конгрессе в таких штатах, как Айова, Огайо и Северная Каролина, где Трамп легко одержал победу два года назад. CNN В этом смысле Ирану, похоже, удалось добиться успеха в своей очевидной попытке использовать промежуточные выборы для нанесения политического ущерба Трампу. Однако ему не удалось превратить это давление в отступление, в результате которого президент завершит войну на его (иранских. — Ред.) условиях, — это одна из причин, по которой нельзя исключать эскалацию со стороны Ирана в ближайшие три недели. Упоминание Трампом избирательного календаря является самым явным свидетельством того, что он осознает негативное влияние войны на кандидатов от его партии на фоне ожесточенной борьбы за контроль над конгрессом. Это также поразительный признак того, что он оказался в ловушке собственной ближневосточной проблемы, которая может иметь разрушительные последствия для его партии и его наследия, так как всего 20 месяцев назад в своей второй инаугурационной речи он обещал, что его успех будет измеряться «войнами, в которые мы никогда не ввязываемся». The Guardian: цены на нефть снижаются после обещания Трампа Цена на нефть марки Brent опустилась примерно на 1% до $103 за баррель после очередной паузы в атаках США на Иран. Цены снизились за ночь на фоне новостей о том, что Трамп пообещал не нападать на Иран в преддверии промежуточных выборов в США, которые состоятся 3 ноября. Это происходит на фоне ослабления общественной поддержки его войны на Ближнем Востоке, что в конечном итоге оказывает давление на избирательные кампании республиканцев. The Guardian Цены на нефть также снизились на фоне новостей о том, что Китай собирается возобновить экспорт топлива после приостановки поставок во время праздника «Золотая неделя». Ожидается, что возобновление экспорта увеличит объемы дизельного топлива, бензина и авиационного топлива на мировом рынке. Обещание Трампа приостановить атаки и возобновление Китаем экспорта топлива нивелируют опасения по поводу возможных перебоев в поставках нефти на побережье Мексиканского залива в США в результате урагана Исайя. Он стал причиной объявления чрезвычайного положения во Флориде, Алабаме и Джорджии. https://en.kabar.kg/news/former-un-human.body: www Kabar South African jurist and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navanethem “Navi” Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law, Qazinform News Agency reports. According to the Norwegian Nobel Committee , Pillay was recognized for her contribution to strengthening international legal institutions and ensuring accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin in Durban, South Africa, during apartheid, Pillay began her legal career challenging racial discrimination and defending anti-apartheid activists, including Nelson Mandela. Throughout her career, she has served as a judge on South Africa’s High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also headed the UN human rights office and chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Pillay currently serves as a judge ad hoc at the International Court of Justice in a case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar over allegations of genocide. The Nobel Committee highlighted Pillay’s role in landmark international cases, particularly at the Rwanda tribunal. “When the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide – her influence was a significant factor,” the committee stated. She also contributed to another legal breakthrough, with a defendant facing charges of incitement to genocide based solely on the dissemination of propaganda for the first time. “Peace requires justice,” the committee stated, stressing the importance of the rule of law in resolving disputes without violence. The French President seems confident that the truce will be agreed in the coming days and that you will be able to resume negotiations. How likely is that and on what terms? -It depends on the position of Armenia. Azerbaijan has always been very supportive to negotiation table, and frankly speaking for 28 years since the OSCE Minsk Group was established we are involved in negotiations. We had hopes and still have hopes that negotiations will lead to progress, and will lead to political settlement. But unfortunately Armenia’s position was opposite. They used negotiation only as a pretext in order to make this process endless. In other words, they wanted always to seal the status quo, to keep status quo unchanged, and not to return the territories back which they have to according to the UN Security Council resolutions and according to the basic principles which are on the table, which were elaborated by the OSCE Minsk Group. Therefore, I hope that after this bitter defeat which Armenia is suffering on the battlefield, they will be more reasonable, and they will listen to the advises of the mediators, and will be sincere on negotiations table. Negotiations should leave to the political settlement, and to the liberation of the occupied territories. -But what territories exactly are we talking about? Are we simply talking about Nagorno-Karabakh or we talking about the seven occupied Azerbaijani territories that they call their security zone? Because clearly you are not getting all of it back. -Our territorial integrity is recognized by the whole world. All the countries recognize territorial integrity of Azerbaijan, which includes Nagorno-Karabakh. Armenians’ position, actually was also a pretext that we are using these seven regions surrounding Nagorno-Karabakh as an excuse to occupy a security zone. But today’s clash shows that there is no security zone in modern world. Modern military equipment does not provide security even for long distance. The security must be provided by political means. Therefore, we were always saying that political settlement will provide security guarantees for all-for Azerbaijanis, for Armenians, for other nationalities who live in the area. And the basic principles which Armenia rejected to support and clearly says how the territories are going to be returned back. In the first stage five regions of Azerbaijan which are situated on the south eastern part of Nagorno-Karabakh. Then two regions of Azerbaijan which are situated between Nagorno-Karabakh and Armenia. Then Azerbaijanis return to Nagorno-Karabakh. There have been 25 percent of Azerbaijanis in Nagorno-Karabakh their rights must also be provided. And they go back to where they lived in the ancient city of Shusha and other places and we restore normal communications, we restore people-to-people contact, and slowly and slowly I am sure people will reconcile. That’s the plan of the mediators and we support it. -Would you recognize Nagorno-Karabakh’s independence if you’re allowed to have 25 percent Azerbaijani population there? -No, no, never. And that has never been the issue on negotiation table. Our position was very clear, that Azerbaijan will never recognize Nagorno-Karabakh’s independence, because it’s our ancient land. The history of Nagorno-Karabakh is now well-known. Second, it is an integral part of Azerbaijan and why should we give independence to small number of people? Azerbaijan is a multi-ethnic country as almost all the countries in the world. National minorities live in peace and dignity in Azerbaijan and in many countries in the world. Я бы даже сказал, что россиян, находящихся на территории Абхазии, мы воспринимаем не как туристов, а как очень близких нам людей. Почему россияне выбирают Абхазию? В первую очередь это наши уникальные природно-климатические условия. Но в не меньшей степени это еще и ментальная близость. Между абхазским и российским народами исторически сложились очень теплые взаимоотношения. Я это видел своими глазами и неоднократно слышал от людей, приезжающих сюда отдохнуть. В Абхазию едут за эмоциями, за человеческим общением. Наши гости стремятся не только насладиться природой, но и окунуться в абхазскую культуру, прочувствовать самобытность, историю нашего народа, нашей земли. Это не просто туризм, это нечто большее. Недавно, например, я общался с одной российской семьей. Они отдыхают в моем родном селе (Ачандара. – «НГ»). Это далеко от моря, в предгорье. Они подружились с одной абхазской семьей там и приезжают туда много лет. Они говорят: «Нам так хорошо здесь, нам даже никакого моря не надо». То есть они наслаждаются не только природой Абхазии, но и вот этими взаимоотношениями, этой дружбой... И обратите внимание, Абхазию ежегодно посещает огромное количество россиян, но, к сожалению, огласку в прессе и соцсетях получают прежде всего негативные инциденты. Хотя если посмотреть на статистику, на количество преступлений на душу населения, то, скажем, в соседнем Сочи показатель примерно такой же (в 2026 году уровень преступности в Абхазии такой же, как в среднем по курортам Юга РФ; по данным начальника штаба МВД Дениса Тания, в первом полугодии 2026 года в Абхазии было совершено 292 преступления, раскрываемость составила 93,2%. – «НГ»). Ежегодное увеличение туристического потока из России в Абхазию – реальный показатель того, что россияне чувствуют себя в нашей республике комфортно и безопасно. Просто здесь мы наблюдаем эффект интернета: 99% туристов уезжают от нас довольными и прекрасно отдохнувшими, но они не пишут отзывов. По поводу того, что нам нужны только богатые туристы – уверяю вас, это все чушь, это неправда. Наше население в целом с невероятной теплотой и уважением относится к нашим дорогим друзьям-россиянам. И мы прекрасно помним, как в тяжелые для нашей республики послевоенные годы к нам приехали первые российские туристы. Это были первопроходцы, и с какой радостью мы их встречали! Они дали нам надежду на возрождение Абхазии как курорта, и все мы здесь очень ждали того времени, когда начнется массовый поток российских туристов. Мы шаг за шагом к этому шли, и сегодня мы изо всех сил стараемся, создаем для наших российских друзей благоприятные условия. В Абхазии за последние годы произошел колоссальный рывок в развитии туристической инфраструктуры. У нас возобновил работу замечательный обновленный аэропорт, налажено железнодорожное сообщение, морское сообщение. Мы делаем все, чтобы россиянам было комфортно добираться до нашей республики. А что касается негативных моментов, мы с каждым случаем работаем. – Если позволите, я задам неудобный вопрос в связи с недавним убийством российской туристки в Гагрском районе. Почему стала возможной эта трагедия? Что происходит с судами Республики Абхазия, со сферой безопасности? Правда ли, что трагедия – результат вмешательства «родственных связей» в вопросы правосудия? Как вы лично видите эту ситуацию? Какие выводы были сделаны руководством страны? Что вы лично планируете делать в республике, чтобы такие трагические случаи больше не повторялись? – Что касается этого страшного, трагического случая, происшедшего недавно... То, о чем вы говорите сейчас, действительно требует особого внимания. Несколько лет тому назад этот гражданин, еще будучи несовершеннолетним, совершил тяжкое преступление (в 2019 году обвиняемый Эдгар Абухба ограбил и изнасиловал туристку из России, на тот момент ему было 17 лет. – «НГ»). Он действительно был освобожден досрочно: в соответствии с действующим абхазским законодательством у него была такая возможность, и его адвокаты воспользовались этим моментом. То есть причина не в коррупции – это случай, когда мы имеем дело с несовершенством законодательной базы. С человеческой точки зрения, конечно же, такого не должно было быть. Он должен был отсидеть весь срок как преступник, совершивший тяжкое преступление. К сожалению, несовершенство нашего законодательства было выявлено в результате трагедии. Иными словами, ссылка на несовершеннолетний возраст оказалась лазейкой для преступника-рецидивиста. По той информации, которая сегодня ко мне поступает, в связи с этим преступником был еще один инцидент в 2025 году, где также была попытка совершения преступления. Тогда сама жертва пожелала скрыть этот факт. Но сегодня ввиду случившейся трагедии и она готова подать заявление на преступника. К сожалению, для семьи погибшей девушки это невосполнимая потеря, а для Абхазии – огромная имиджевая потеря. Мы, конечно же, сделали выводы и планируем вносить соответствующие законодательные инициативы по ужесточению наказания для такого рода преступников. Главное, что я хочу сказать: Абхазия – правовое государство и для нас в приоритете – верховенство закона. Подавляющее большинство туристов в Абхазии – из России. Фото РИА Новости – Ситуация с Грузией – какие вы видите здесь перспективы? Грузино-абхазская война 1992–1993 годов официально не закончена, мирный договор не подписан, Тбилиси считает Абхазию частью своей территории. Появится ли в обозримом будущем мирный договор или хотя бы соглашение о ненападении, которого Абхазия ожидает много лет? – Взаимоотношения с Грузией остаются непростыми. Мы все послевоенные годы регулярно ставим вопрос о подписании соглашения о ненападении, о неприменении силы, но, к сожалению, до сих пор этого соглашения нет. Конечно же, мы не хотим конфронтации, возобновления боевых действий, потому что это будет катастрофа и для абхазского, и для грузинского народов. И я очень надеюсь, что все политики будут предельно осторожны в своих высказываниях на эту тему. При этом мы занимаемся вопросами обороноспособности нашей страны. Абхазская армия, при всех наших сложностях, укрепляется. И конечно же, колоссальную роль играет поддержка российского военного контингента и взаимодействие между министерствами обороны Республики Абхазия и Российской Федерации. Именно это позволяет сегодня обеспечить безопасность нашего государства. Что касается Грузии, уверен, что приоритетом для властей этой страны должны быть интересы грузинского народа. Не думаю, что в интересах грузинского народа появление еще одной горячей точки на Кавказе. – Вы верите, что в течение вашего президентского срока Грузия подпишет договор о ненападении – исходя из той риторики, которую мы слышим сегодня? – Лично я считаю, что как раз сейчас самое вре

https://iz.ru/2180875/vladislav-daniilov.body: Товары, не прошедшие контроль качества, попадают в российские магазины и на маркетплейсы под прикрытием высокопоставленных чиновников ЕАЭС, выяснили «Известия». По версии источников издания, они действуют в интересах десятков лабораторий, которые без всяких тестов и исследований оформляют документы, якобы подтверждающие качество продукции. По фактам выдачи 15 тыс. таких сертификатов организациями из Армении и Киргизии уже возбуждены уголовные дела. За лоббированием интересов подобных структур, по информации «Известий», может стоять министр ЕЭК по внутренним рынкам Варос Симонян. Его уже публично обвиняли в фактическом саботаже полноценного внедрения Интегрированной информационной системы ЕАЭС, нацеленной на борьбу с контрафактом. Как устроены схемы, позволяющие армянским псевдолабораториям не прекращать работу даже после отзыва лицензий, и почему высокопоставленный чиновник ЕАЭС препятствует обелению товарооборота между странами — в расследовании «Известий». Серые сертификаты из ЕАЭС С 1 октября в России вступили в силу новые правила работы цифровых платформ. Теперь, чтобы реализовать товары на маркетплейсах, продавцу недостаточно предоставить скан сертификата о проверке его качества. Все эти документы будут проверяться через межгосударственные базы данных — подлинный ли сертификат, не аннулирован ли он. Фото: ИЗВЕСТИЯ/Сергей Лантюхов Ужесточение правил связано с существованием на рынке огромного количества поддельных документов или выданных законно только формально, а на самом деле — без реальной проверки качества товаров. В России борьба за обеление рынка сертификации ведется давно. Первыми ее результатами стало закрытие отечественных лабораторий, выдававших фиктивные сертификаты, — это происходило в том числе после расследований «Известий». Так, летом 2024 года наши журналисты передали центру «Сертификейшн групп» документы на созданные в виртуальной реальности кроссовки и спокойно получили сертификат качества на них — по результатам якобы проведенных испытаний. В результате Роскачество начало тотальные проверки всех сертификационных центров, у некоторых лицензии были аннулированы . Внеблоковое мышление: ЕАЭС обретает новых партнеров на внешних рынках Переговоры ведутся с Индией и Тунисом — кто еще проявляет интерес к сотрудничеству с союзом И вот теперь выяснилось, что большая их часть продолжила свою деятельность, перерегистрировавшись в других странах ЕАЭС, в основном в Киргизии и Армении. В мае 2025 года Владимир Путин по итогам встречи с представителями деловых кругов поручил правительству аннулировать сертификаты на товары из стран — членов ЕАЭС, выданные с нарушениями. 23 декабря Росаккредитация заблокировала на территории РФ первые 13 сертификатов и деклараций о соответствии, оформленных с нарушениями: иностранные центры сертификации не предоставили результаты лабораторных исследований товаров. Фото: ТАСС/Роман Храмовник Первыми под приостановку попали сертификаты на детские игрушки, одежду и обувь — товары высокого социального спроса. Справка «Известий» В России для ряда товаров перед выпуском в продажу необходимо подтвердить их соответствие установленным требованиям безопасности. Для этого продукция проходит оценку, а в предусмотренных случаях — испытания в аккредитованных лабораториях. Такие требования распространяются на автомобили и комплектующие, бытовую технику и электронику, одежду и обувь, парфюмерию и косметику, бытовую химию, мебель, детские товары, игрушки и пищевую продукцию. По итогам проверки оформляется сертификат соответствия или другой предусмотренный для конкретного товара разрешительный документ. Проводить испытания и выдавать сертификаты могут только организации, имеющие соответствующую аккредитацию. Для импортной продукции во многих случаях действуют единые требования Евразийского экономического союза. Товар проверяют на соответствие техрегламентам ЕАЭС, а сертификацию и испытания проводят организации, включенные в единый реестр союза. При этом документ, оформленный в одной из стран ЕАЭС по единым требованиям, действует и в остальных государствах объединения. В феврале 2026 года Росаккредитация сообщила , что прекратила действие на территории России всех документов трех киргизских центров сертификации — «Мурас», «Центр сертификации и испытаний», «Эксперт-Лайн». В 2025 году только три эти центра выдали российским компаниям более 15,5 тыс. сертификатов. — На сегодня по фактам выдачи 15 тыс. сертификатов возбуждены уголовные дела. Под ответственность попали 11 лабораторий, из которых 10 зарегистрированы в Киргизии, а одна — в Армении, — сообщил «Известиям» источник, близкий к правоохранительным органам. Фото: ИЗВЕСТИЯ/Дмитрий Коротаев В июле 2026 года Росаккредитация прекратила действие некоторых сертификатов, выданных теперь уже армянскими центрами «АРМТЕСТ» и «АРМ-ТЕСТ». Причина та же — отсутствие какого-либо ответа на запрос российской стороны о предоставлении протоколов испытаний на продукцию. — До недавнего времени Росаккредитация физически не имела права в одностороннем порядке аннулировать или приостанавливать действие документов, выданных в других государствах союза, даже если знала о нарушениях. Это считалось бы нарушением суверенитета национальной системы аккредитации другой страны. Ситуация изменилась только в конце прошлого года, когда ведомство получило расширенные полномочия, — пояснил «Известиям» председатель Общественной потребительской инициативы Олег Павлов. Речь идет о постановлении правительства России, по которому Росаккредитация получила право приостанавливать на территории РФ действие сертификатов и деклараций из других стран ЕАЭС. Продажа сертификатов и деклараций соответствия ЕАЭС российским заказчикам в Армении фактически превратилась в отлаженный бизнес. Документ, выданный аккредитованным армянским органом по сертификации, действует на всей территории союза, а значит позволяет легально ввозить и продавать товар в России. При этом для российских заказчиков армянские сертификаты, как правило, обходятся дешевле, чем российские. Различные площадки предлагают услуги сертификации продукции в Армении от 2 тыс. рублей «под ключ». Фото: ИЗВЕСТИЯ Пример стоимости услуг за оформление сертификата соответствия в Армении При этом сами испытания нередко могут и вовсе не проводиться. Если армянский регулятор приостанавливает или прекращает действие аттестата аккредитации одного органа, на его месте почти сразу появляется другой: с новым названием и новым юрлицом, но с теми же руководителями — «Известиям» удалось проследить сразу несколько таких цепочек. На одного человека бывает оформлено несколько органов по сертификации. Такие запасные площадки позволяют не прерывать работу, даже если у одного из органов отзовут аккредитацию. Фото: ИЗВЕСТИЯ Пример создания цепочки сертификационных центров, оформленных на одних и тех же людей Кто стоит за серым рынком сертификации Обязанность вести единый реестр товаров, требующих сертификации, возложена на Евразийскую экономическую комиссию (ЕЭК) — постоянно действующий наднациональный регулирующий орган ЕАЭС. За сферу сертификации отвечает Варос Симонян , занимающий в ЕЭК пост министра по внутренним рынкам, информатизации, информационно-коммуникационным технологиям. Он делегирован в организацию от Армении. — Судя по всему, выдача серых сертификатов была поставлена в Армении на поток еще когда Варос Симонян работал в министерстве экономики республики (в 2019–2021 годах занимал пост заместителя министра. — «Известия»). Там он, до перехода в ЕЭК, курировал деятельность Национального органа по аккредитации Армении (ARMNAB), — рассказал источник «Известий». Прийти к разногласию: Армения вынесла торговый спор с РФ на площадку ЕАЭС На что пожаловался Пашинян и к чему пришли участники саммита в Киргизии По мнению нашего собеседника, именно Симонян мог повлиять на фактический срыв сроков внедрения Интегрированной информационной системы (ИИС) — единого цифрового сервиса услуг в рамках ЕАЭС, который заметно упростил бы и процесс отслеживания актуальности сертификатов качества товаров

https://www.rfa.org/english/uyghur/2026/.body: Updated June 12, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT A Bangkok court on Thursday sentenced two Uyghur men to death for triggering a bomb explosion which killed twenty and injured over a hundred others over a decade ago. “The deaths and injuries caused by the attack were a terrible tragedy, and the victims and their families deserve justice,” Rebiya Kadeer of the International Uyghur Human Rights and Democracy Foundation (IUHRDF) told RFA. “However, justice cannot be achieved through proceedings that leave significant questions unanswered regarding due process, the treatment of defendants , and the reliability of key evidence,” Kadeer added. uyghuyr-bomb-suspect-thailand-trial_0 Forensic officials and rescue foundation volunteers clean up the Erawan Shrine in Bangkok, a day after the bomb explosion killed 20 people, Aug. 18, 2015. (RFA) No group claimed responsibility for the Erawan Shrine bombing in central Bangkok on Aug. 17, 2015, but speculation called it an act of retaliation against the forced deportation of more than 109 Uyghurs from Thailand a month earlier. Shortly after the bombing, Thai police named 17 suspects. Arrested were two Uyghurs, Adem Karadag (alias Bilal Mohammed) and Yusufu Mieraili, who went on trial in 2016 for planting explosives. Both have denied all charges brought against them Upon hearing the verdict delivered by a four-judge panel on Thursday, Mieraili shouted “Injustice!” in the courtroom in both English and Thai. “RIP Thailand’s justice system. I don’t accept any of this,” Mieraili added. “I didn’t do anything wrong.” uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Adem Karadag (alias Bilal Mohammed), left, and Yusufu Mieraili during a Feb.16, 2016, appearance at a Thai military court. (Nicolas Asfouri/AFP) During the trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Mieraili and Karadag had been near the shrine around the time of the explosion, that they had communicated with each other by telephone, and that a taxi driver had transported them away from the area after the incident. The judges stated that although the defendants had denied committing the crime, they had failed to refute the evidence presented against them. The court granted both men 30 days to file an appeal. Defense lawyer Choochat Kanpai told reporters they “will appeal the ruling because there are many aspects of the case that the court has not fully considered, including the treatment of the defendants during the proceedings.” The decade-long trial was beset by delays due to the coronavirus pandemic and problems securing translators. uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Defense lawyers speak to reporters at Bangkok South Criminal Court, June 11, 2026, after the verdict for the Erawan Shrine bombing. (Lillian Suwanrumpha/AFP) Seven Chinese tourists were among the fatalities when explosives—apparently left in a backpack—detonated. Beijing welcomed the death sentences. “The attackers were totally inhumane and extremely heinous,” foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters. “China supports Thailand in conducting the trial in accordance with the law and severely punishing the murderers.” Bahtiyar Bora of the Australian Uyghur Association who provided assistance and translation for Karadag and Mieraili during court proceedings in Thailand, spoke to RFA about China’s response to the verdict. “These two Uyghurs fled Chinese oppression and came to Thailand. China is, of course, pleased with their severe punishment and can continue to accuse Uyghurs of terrorism internationally,” Bora said. Thailand deported 40 Uyghurs to China in February 2025 despite warnings from human rights groups that they would face persecution on their return, drawing swift condemnation from the United Nations. uyghur-bangkok-erawan-shrine-bombing-verdict Rebiya Kadeer at the fourth General Assembly of the World Uyghur Congress in Tokyo May 14, 2012. (Yuriko Nakao/Reuters) “These actions have reinforced concerns that decisions involving Uyghurs in Thailand may be influenced by political and economic considerations linked to Beijing rather than by international human rights obligations,” Rebiya Kadeer told RFA. “Against this background, it is difficult for many in the Uyghur community to have confidence that this verdict was reached entirely free from political influence,” Kadeer said. Adds quote from Bahtiyar Bora of the Australian Uyghur Association. Pimuk Rakkanam reported from Bangkok, Tahir Hamut Izgil reported from Washington. With reporting from AFP and Reuters. Edited by Charlie Dharapak.

https://hrf.org/latest/imprisoned-karaka.body: @HRF View post Dauletmurat Tazhimuratov, a prisoner of conscience in Uzbekistan, has shared a letter from prison detailing the abuse and severe mistreatment he is suffering while incarcerated. Tazhimuratov is a Karakalpak lawyer, journalist, and human rights defender who has been detained in Uzbekistan since July 2022, when the Uzbek government cracked down on protesters who opposed constitutional amendments that would have stripped Karakalpakstan of its status as a sovereign republic. Writing from detention, Tazhimuratov describes brutal beatings he has received at the hands of prison officials, who force him to recite the Uzbek national anthem or deny his Karakalpak identity by declaring that he is Uzbek. He is also denied access to bathing facilities, medical care, writing materials, and religious items. HRF calls on Uzbekistan to treat Dauletmurat Tazhimuratov with dignity and recognize his fundamental rights by providing him with access to basic necessities and investigating all incidents of violence against him. Most of all, the Uzbek government must enforce the opinion of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention and release him from prison immediately. View post

https://www.rfa.org/english/uyghur/2025/.body: A new report says major Chinese producers of critical minerals are using state-imposed forced labor programs in the Uyghur region to meet rising global demand, putting international brands they export to at risk of complicity in human rights violations. According to the report by Hague-based rights group Global Rights Compliance , 77 companies and downstream manufacturers of critical minerals-based products operate in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), placing them at risk of participation in the labor transfer programs in the lithium, titanium, beryllium, and magnesium industries. The findings are likely to add to the due diligence concerns of foreign and multinational companies that source those products. Forced labor is on a long list of serious human rights problems that have been documented in Xinjiang, where the U.S. government determined in 2021 that China was committing genocide against the Uyghurs. The Uyghur region is a major source of four critical minerals. It is the top source of beryllium, crucial for nuclear applications and advanced electronics, and one of the five province-level jurisdictions that produces raw magnesium. The region is also seeing a surge in lithium exploration, mining, and battery production to feed the electric vehicle industry, and accounts for 11.6% of the world’s titanium sponge, a key input in titanium metal that is used in aerospace and defense. Over the past decade, Beijing has expanded exploration, mining, processing and manufacturing of critical minerals in the XUAR, transforming the region into a major “extractive hub,” Global Rights Compliance said in its report titled “Risk at the Source: Critical Mineral Supply Chains and State-Imposed Forced Labor in the Uyghur Region.” China dominates global mineral production. The country leads production of 30 out of the 44 minerals that the U.S. government has designated as critical. uyghur-rare-earths The June 2025 Global Rights Compliance report on mineral supply chains and forced labor in the Uyghur region. (Global Rights Compliance) “The emergence of the region as an extractive hub relies, in part, on state-imposed forced labor transfer programs, targeting Uyghurs and other Turkic ethnic groups,” the rights group said. The report highlights the “substantial influence” that these critical minerals – found abundantly in XUAR – have on global supply chains and multinational brands, including leading paint companies, aerospace applications, thermos producers, and defense and nuclear tools and components. It uncovers 15 companies with documented sourcing directly from Uyghur region-based companies in the last two years and 68 downstream customers of Chinese producers who source inputs from the Uyghur region, highlighting the risk of companies’ direct and indirect participation in the forced labor programs. “The XUAR’s systemic forced labor practices are not only a means to subsidize operating costs but also facilitate the government’s persecution of the Uyghur population through familial separation, land expropriation, and forced re-education,” Global Rights Alliance said. The report highlights that China’s practices in the Uyghur region create unfair competitive advantages and trade and environmental violations that extend beyond human rights concerns. Lax environmental standards and heavy dependence on coal have also made the region the epicenter of the energy-intensive mineral mining and processing industry and have enabled goods to enter global markets at artificially low prices, it said. “Minerals mined and/or refined in the region routinely enter global supply chains through unregulated or opaque mineral distribution channels. As a result, significant portions of the world’s economy are potentially exposed to products tainted by forced labor and high carbon footprints,” the rights group added. The report’s findings were based on analyses of state media, shipping records, and marketing and corporate annual reports. Edited by Mat Pennington.

WASHINGTON — The House passed the Uyghur Policy Act on Tuesday, a bill that advances a strategy for the United States to support Uyghurs and other ethnic minorities enduring persecution at the hands of China’s government. It’s the latest try for the measure, which was passed by the House in the past two congressional terms without advancing further. Sponsored by a bipartisan group led by Rep. Young Kim, a California Republican, and Rep. Ami Bera, a California Democrat, the measure calls on the State Department to oversee Uyghur human rights-related policies and programs that preserve Uyghurs’ ethnic, religious, cultural and linguistic identities. The Uyghur people have been imprisoned, tortured, & brainwashed at the hands of the Chinese Communist Party. I spoke on the House floor in favor of my Uyghur Policy Act — so we can show through words & actions that we stand against the CCP's heinous crimes. pic.twitter.com/QU3JhwutIc — Young Kim (@RepYoungKim) September 2, 2025 The bill aims to increase accountability for human rights organizations and sets a strategy to close detention facilities and political reeducation camps in China. It also creates reporting mechanisms for Uyghur victims. “For too long, the Chinese Communist Party has orchestrated the forced sterilization, enslavement, and systematic murder of the Uyghur people,” Kim said in a statement. “The United States cannot sit idly by as innocent families are torn apart, identities are erased, and generations silenced by these atrocious acts of genocide.” Rushan Abbas , executive director of the Campaign for Uyghurs and chair of the executive committee of the World Uyghur Congress, said the measure was a “vital step to ensure America stands firmly with the Uyghur people amid China’s ongoing genocide.” “By making Uyghur human rights a clear priority in U.S. foreign policy, this bill strengthens accountability for the Chinese government’s crimes and delivers a powerful message of solidarity to millions of Uyghur families suffering under repression,” she said.

A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers this week announced a bill that would broaden existing sanctions to combat what one senator called “a deliberate and systematic campaign to destroy the Uyghur people” — one of a set of bills targeting China over its treatment of minority groups, dissidents and Taiwan as bilateral trade negotiations continue. The measure would expand the sanctions under a previous law to include actions like forced family separations and organ harvesting . It would also deny entry to the U.S. for people found to have participated in forced abortions or sterilizations . In interviews with RFA Uyghur , Uyghur women have detailed birth control procedures they say were forced on them by authorities in northwest China’s Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. The bill would bar the U.S. military from buying Chinese seafood out of concern that Uyghur and North Korean forced labor is used in its production. It would direct the State Department to create a plan for countering Chinese propaganda that denies “the genocide, crimes against humanity, and other egregious human rights abusese experienced by Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim ethic groups” in Xinjiang. It would also appropriate $2 million for the Smithsonian to create research and programs that would preserve Uyghur language and culture threatened by the Chinese government . “The evidence is clear. The Chinese Communist Party has waged a deliberate and systematic campaign to destroy the Uyghur people through forced sterilization, mass internment, and forced labor,” Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), the chairman of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China and one of the bill’s co-sponsors, said in a statement. “This legislation ensures the United States holds accountable not only the perpetrators of these horrific crimes but also those who support or profit from them.” Joining Sullivan in co-sponsoring the bill are Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Rep. Tom Suozzi (D-N.Y.), and Rep. John Moolenaar (R-Mich.). Rushan Abbas, executive director of the Campaign for Uyghurs, a U.S.-based nonprofit advocacy group, and the chairwoman of the Executive Committee of the World Uyghur Congress, an international organization promoting Uyghur rights, said the measure’s introduction is “a critical step toward dismantling the systems of control and repression that have enabled genocide and devastated Uyghur families and communities.” “For Uyghurs who have endured years of silence and separation, this bill represents a meaningful step toward exposing the truth, advancing justice, and creating pathways to family reunification,” Abbas told RFA. U.S. lawmakers this week also planned to release a bill that would aim to help Taiwan and support countries that maintain official diplomatic relations with its government, as well as a measure to combat efforts by any foreign government to reach beyond its borders to intimidate, harass or harm activists, dissidents or journalists. In response to the bills, China’s foreign ministry on Tuesday rejected U.S. accusations on Xinjiang and Taiwan. “The related accusations are entirely fabricated and are malicious slander,” the ministry said. The measures come as an Aug. 12 deadline looms for a durable trade deal between the U.S. and China. A U.S. official told reporters that progress is being made toward a deal, Reuters reported Friday. Includes reporting by Reuters.

https://www.rfa.org/english/uyghur/2026/.body: Human rights and Taiwan are “red lines” for China that cannot be crossed, the country’s ambassador to the U.S. warned on Wednesday, ahead of President Xi Jinping’s arrival in Washington for a three-day summit. Chinese Ambassador Xie Feng, writing in the ruling Communist Party’s official People’s Daily, said managing differences hinges on good faith, and the U.S. should stop “fabricating pretexts” such as national security, economic imbalances and forced labor to try to constrain China. “China’s sovereignty, security, and development interests cannot be violated, and four red lines — the Taiwan question, democracy and human rights, development paths and systems, and development rights — cannot be challenged,” Xie said. RFA Uyghur’s Shohret Hoshur interviewed Rebiya Kadeer of the Washington-based International Uyghur Human Rights and Democracy Foundation (IUHRDF) for her reaction to China’s “red lines” statement ahead of Xi’s meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump . The interview has been edited for length and clarity. RFA: Why do you think Beijing issued this warning at this particular moment? Rebiya Kadeer: The Uyghur genocide and human rights issue is China’s greatest vulnerability. It is also a crime that China has spent enormous financial resources attempting to conceal from the international community. At this important moment, when the world is paying close attention, China does not want this vulnerability to be exposed. RFA: Do you interpret the warning as a sign that Beijing fears President Trump may raise what his administration has called the Uyghur genocide and individual Uyghur political-prisoner cases during his meeting with Xi Jinping? If so, what does it reveal about Beijing’s concerns? Rebiya Kadeer: Ahead of Xi Jinping’s visit, several members of Congress called on President Trump to raise the cases of political prisoners—including Gulshan Abbas, Ilham Tohti, Rahile Dawut and Ekpar Asat—and demand their release. China knows that, in a democratic country such as the United States, the views of members of Congress carry weight and receive serious attention. Therefore, through this statement, China is attempting to pressure President Trump. RFA: Does this warning demonstrate confidence—or fear that China’s human-rights abuses could become part of the summit negotiations? Rebiya Kadeer: This is certainly not the kind of statement made by a strong country. China’s economic development is not healthy development; it has been built upon unfair competition and coercion. The stability China has established within the country, particularly in East Turkistan (Xinjiang in Chinese), is not natural stability—it is artificially imposed stability. Therefore, although the Chinese government may appear strong, it is fundamentally weak. A government that fears its own people and is unable to embrace democratic elections is a fearful government. It is especially afraid of criticism. RFA: How should President Trump respond to Beijing’s effort to place human rights outside the summit discussions? Rebiya Kadeer: China’s statement itself demonstrates why President Trump must raise the Uyghur genocide and human rights. I believe that raising these issues would give President Trump the upper hand at the negotiating table and help him achieve his objectives on other matters. If he does not raise them, he will not only be acting against the will of the American people, but he will also lose ground on the other issues under negotiation. I call upon—and hope—President Trump will follow a course befitting the strong president of a powerful country. With reporting by Reuters. Edited by Charlie Dharapak.
